gw.inn: HTTP request from a harness: bearer token or x-api-key, anthropic-beta header, JSON body.

Attach a request id and session id to every upstream call and log row.
Pull the signed policy bundle on a timer and keep the last good copy.

algorithm.name: Route, resolve, reserve, forward, tee
algorithm.formula: allow = key_valid AND policy_ok AND reserve_ok; else 401, 403, 402 or 429
steps: Match the route prefix to a wire protocol.
Call authk with the credential; reject with 401 if unknown.
Load the policy bundle and the fmode rule for this route.
Ask bres for a worst-case hold; on refusal return 402.
Open the upstream stream via the connector and start the tee.
Stream bytes to the client unchanged.
On stream end or error, hand usage to norm and release or true up the hold.

params.forwarded_headers: anthropic-beta, anthropic-version, x-grok-conv-id, x-session-id [C:052, A:221, A:231]

security: Admin and tenant tokens are separate from provider keys; provider keys come from the vault at call time.
Redact Authorization, x-api-key and cookie headers from every log line.
Terminate TLS (transport layer security) and refuse plain HTTP outside localhost.
Reject bodies above a size cap to stop memory exhaustion (DevX proposal).

performance.slo: Under 50 ms added at p95 before first byte (DevX proposal).
performance.complexity: O(1) per request plus the stream copy, which is O(bytes).
performance.scaling: Stateless instances behind a load balancer; session stickiness is by key hash, not by instance.

edge_cases: Client sends anthropic-beta with a value Token Economics does not know: forward it unchanged.
Upstream closes the stream mid-response: return what was sent, log usage_missing, bill the hold as an estimate.
Policy bundle is stale or unsigned: keep the last good bundle, alert, never accept an unsigned one.
Client disconnects after the upstream charged: the tee keeps reading usage to the end.
Subscription OAuth token arrives: hand to b_oauth and mark auth_mode subscription.

algorithm.name: Side-copy usage parser

steps: Write the chunk to the client socket first.
Append a bounded copy to the parse buffer.
On message_delta, response.completed or the last SSE (server-sent events) chunk, parse usage.
Record headers: request id, rate-limit remaining, service tier.
Emit the raw usage object plus ids to norm.

security: Drop content blocks from the buffer once usage is parsed.

Bound the buffer to stop memory growth from a hostile stream.
